# Matching and rule IDs

Every finding carries a `rule` and a `reason`. The rule says which step decided the category. Matching tries the keys in order: identity, then ARN, then normalized ID, and the first that finds a state resource decides. Unmapped types are `undetermined`, never managed. `<name>` stands for a rule or preset name.

| Rule | Commands | Category | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match/identity` | scan, whois | managed | A state resource has the same resource identity (account, region and the identity attributes). |
| `match/arn` | scan, whois | managed | A state resource has the same ARN. |
| `match/id` | scan, whois | managed | A state resource has the same normalized ID. |
| `match/rule-tuple` | scan | managed | An `aws_security_group_rule` has the same protocol, ports, source and direction. |
| `match/inline-rule` | scan | managed | An inline `ingress` or `egress` block of an `aws_security_group` has the same tuple. |
| `match/parent-in-state` | scan | derived | No state has the resource, but a state manages its parent, which creates it. |
| `match/double-managed` | scan, whois | double-managed | Instances in more than one state match the resource. |
| `match/no-type-mapping` | scan, whois | undetermined | The type has no mapping to a Terraform type, so tfcensus can't tell whether a state manages it ([type coverage](/reference/type-coverage)). |
| `match/ambiguous` | whois | undetermined | Instances of different Terraform types have the ARN or ID. Narrow the query with `--type`. |
| `match/not-in-state` | scan | unmanaged | No state manages the resource and no ownership rule matched it. Findings carry `rules/no-match` once the rules ran. |
| `rules/no-match` | scan | unmanaged | No built-in pack and no user rule matched the unmanaged resource. |
| `pack/<pack>/<name>` | scan, whois | the pack's | A rule of a built-in pack matched ([rule packs](/reference/rule-packs)). |
| `guard/<name>` | scan | unmanaged | A guard kept a user rule from hiding the resource ([guards](/reference/rule-packs#guards)). |
| `user/<name>` | scan, whois, drift | the rule's | Your rule in `rules` (scan, whois) or `drift.noise` (drift) matched. |
| `inherit/<category>` | scan | the parent's | The resource took its parent's category, such as an IAM role policy of an AWS-managed role. `scan --explain` shows the parent chain. |
| `source/cloudformation` | scan | other-iac | A CloudFormation stack lists the resource and no state manages it. |
| `whois/not-found` | whois --live | unmanaged | A state has the ARN or ID, but the live inventory listed the type and the resource isn't there. |
| `preset/<name>` | drift | hidden | A [drift noise preset](/reference/drift-noise) hid the change. |

Backend audit findings carry the check ID as their rule, such as `S3-VER` ([audit checks](/reference/audit-checks)).
